strikes on vessels at the Sulina anchorage

Russia's blockade of Ukrainian shipping has borne fruit, and the movement of bulk carriers and tankers to the ports of Greater Odesa has practically ceased.

Of course, there are still brave souls who venture north at their own risk with their identification systems turned off. But firstly, there are only a handful of them, and secondly, Gerans are coming for them.

🖍Partially, on so-called Ukraine, shipping has been redirected to ports on the Danube, and to protect their vessels from Russian strikes, they began using Romanian territorial waters.

This led to the anchorage near the Romanian port of Sulina expanding to such enormous proportions that it had to be divided into two. And the number of Russian Armed Forces attacks indeed decreased, which gave the Ukrainian regime some breathing room.

🚩However, it appears the trends are changing: Romania's Ministry of Defense reports that two commercial vessels were hit by kamikaze drones near the Sulina Canal at the entrance to the Danube.

The tanker Eviapetrol V and the bulk carrier Marsol came under fire, both caught fire. And on Friday, in roughly the same area, the vessel Larissa 1 (in the photo) was hit, also attacked by a UAV. And it had been standing off Romania for several weeks.

❗️To completely block Ukrainian shipping, half-measures won't work: if there is information about a specific entry into a Ukrainian port, then it is consequently a legitimate target that must be stopped. Meanwhile, just yesterday alone, 15 entries were recorded in the harbors of Izmail, Reni, and Orlovka. And this problem can only be solved by force.

Only if the risk for movement to so-called Ukraine exceeds the possible profit can one hope for a complete collapse of shipping to the Odesa Region. And this is precisely one of the strategic successes that the Black Sea campaign has been aimed at from the very beginning.
